purpose: A census of the `paper`-prefixed declaration names in DavisKahan, and a mechanically applicable rename proposal. Stage A -- the one-sided renames whose targets were unoccupied -- IS APPLIED; see `application_log` and `stage_status` for exactly what, and what remains.
motivation: The 2026-09-01 rename replaced `PaperUnitaryInvariantNorm` with `SymmetricNormingFunction` because the name recorded provenance where the mathematics had its own name. That decision was never generalised, and `paper` is not in the naming classification's banned-token list, so the rest of the family was left in place. Measured here: of the declarations carrying the token, the great majority contrast with nothing -- there is no other `blockCompression`, `diagonalPair`, or `projectorDifference` in the tree -- so the prefix distinguishes nothing and reads as unfinished. ForTauCeti, the permanent product, already carries none of these names.

policy.provenance_only: The token distinguishes nothing: no declaration of the stripped name exists. Proposed action is to drop the prefix. These are mechanical.
policy.contrastive_decision_required: A declaration of the stripped name already exists, so the prefix currently carries meaning. Each of these needs a human decision -- which spelling is canonical, and what the other becomes -- and MUST NOT be renamed mechanically.
policy.dependent_declaration_names: Declarations whose own names begin with the renamed one. They have to move in the same commit, or a lemma stops matching the object it is about.
policy.not_covered: Prose. Docstrings and audit narratives say 'the paper's ...' in the ordinary English sense, which is correct and stays. Only declaration names are proposed here.

application_notes: Statement pins under `.leanq/` regenerate; they are not edited by hand.

`Challenge/**` and `comparator/*.json` hold declaration names as data and are not compiled by a default build. Run `python3 scripts/check_declaration_name_drift.py` and `lake build Challenge` after applying.
`Audits/ResultSemanticSurface.lean` names every canonical declaration; the result-inventory checker rejects a canonical declaration missing from it.

Re-pin statements and re-stamp `semantic_review_sweep.canonical_evidence_sha256` from the post-rename data, and record in the inventory review that the change is rename-only, with the evidence for that claim.

This is the hazard that would bite hardest -- `hilbertSchmidtNorm` and `projectionBlock` are the kind of name Mathlib might already own -- and it is clear.

verification.method: Declaration heads parsed from every .lean file under DavisKahan/ and ForTauCeti/; occurrence counts are word-boundary matches per surface. Counts are evidence of blast radius, not a substitute for applying the rename and rebuilding.
verification.angle_family_finding: Checked directly, 2026-09-02. The `paper*` angle operators are the functional calculus of the angle: `paperCosAngleOperatorC = cfc Real.cos (paperAngleOperatorC U V)`, and similarly for sin, tan, sin 2, tan 2. The existing UNPREFIXED names are different constructions built on the directed sine: `cosAngleOperatorC = modulus (P_V ∘L P_U)`, `sinTwoAngleOperatorC = 2 • (sinAngleOperatorDirectedC * cosAngleOperatorC)`, and `tanAngleOperatorC` composes `sinAngleOperatorDirectedC` with an inverse cosine equivalence and additionally takes an acuteness hypothesis. So the unqualified names currently denote the directed objects while the canonical functional-calculus objects carry a provenance prefix. That is the inconsistency the collision exposed, and it is why the resolution is to normalise the family rather than rename around it.
verification.cited_names_present: All 52 declarations named in the amended families were confirmed to exist in the tree before being written here.
verification.embedded_token_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-02. The original census matched only LEADING `paper`/`Paper`/`IsPaper`, so declaration names carrying the token after an underscore or inside camelCase were never enumerated. A follow-up census found 144 such names, 96 of them mechanically stale -- the object had been renamed by stage A and the theorem name had not, so `adjoint_paperBlockCompression` stated a fact about `blockCompression`. This field previously reported no embedded-token residue; that claim was false, and it was false because the census did not look. 83 of the 96 were repaired on 2026-09-02; the remaining 13 are blocked on the stage B angle family and the stage C Hilbert-Schmidt decision, and will fall out of those. A further 9 names were reached on 2026-09-02 by deriving inner tokens from `Is`/`Has`-prefixed renames; see the `stage_a_inner_token_residue` log entry.

not_yet_decided: Stage A is applied. What remains undecided is the ORDER and content of stages B and C, for which the reviewer has given a recommended sequence: embedded-token residue, then the angle family atomically, then selected-branch tan 2Theta, then the Hilbert-Schmidt and plane migrations.

The angle-family normalisation moves EXISTING unprefixed declarations, so it is a two-sided rename and cannot be applied by the mechanical map alone; it needs its own pass with a build after each family.
Whether the Hilbert--Schmidt and plane consolidations happen as part of this campaign or as separate migrations, since they delete concepts rather than rename them.

Whether the `*RC` angle variants should keep wrapping the directed complex objects, or be re-pointed at the literal ones so that the R and RC families agree. That is a change of statement and needs a mathematical decision, not a rename.
policy_statement: Provenance goes in namespaces, modules, docstrings, and source-census metadata. A permanent declaration name describes the mathematical object, or the representation that distinguishes it from another object. Resolving a collision is therefore never a matter of finding a different prefix: where two names collide, the collision is usually exposing an API distinction that should be settled.
amendment_note: Amended on hostile review of the first proposal. The mechanical pass stripped `paper` and stopped, which would have preserved several latent defects under new spellings: it left the DIRECTED angle constructions holding the unqualified names, produced `source*` names that are still provenance, left `paper` embedded mid-name in theorem names whose prefix alone was stripped, and proposed competing for names the canonical ForTauCeti API already owns. The families below replace the mechanical proposal wherever they overlap it.

families.title: Canonical angle-function objects take the unqualified names; the directed constructions say `directed`.
families.rationale: The unqualified names currently hold the directed/product constructions while the canonical functional-calculus objects carry a provenance prefix. Swapping them gives a predictable API -- angleOperatorC, sinAngleOperatorC, cosAngleOperatorC, tanAngleOperatorC, sinTwoAngleOperatorC, tanTwoAngleOperatorC and their directed* siblings -- and puts the qualifier on the construction that is genuinely special. This is a two-sided rename: several EXISTING unprefixed declarations move, so it cannot be applied by stripping prefixes.

families.title: Consolidate into the canonical ForTauCeti API rather than renaming.
families.rationale: `ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidt`, `hilbertSchmidtEnergy` and `hilbertSchmidtENorm` already exist and are canonical, and the repository has already proved that the source-side approximation-singular-value definitions describe the same notion. Renaming the paper copies into those names would compete with the canonical API; the polished end state migrates consumers to it and deletes the duplicate concept, keeping the mathematics as characterisation theorems. Any intermediate that must survive the migration is named for what distinguishes it, `singularValueHilbertSchmidtEnergy` / `singularValueHilbertSchmidtNorm`, not for the canonical name.

moves.fallback: singularValueHilbertSchmidtNorm, only if an intermediate is needed during migration

families.title: One canonical name for the two-dimensional model space.
families.rationale: `Plane` is too generic to be a reusable name and the aliases add nothing. One name, `PlanarModelSpace 𝕜` for `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin 2)`, used as `PlanarModelSpace ℝ` and `PlanarModelSpace ℂ`. Role-bearing model names replace `planeE0`-style names.

families.title: Name the extra data, not its provenance.
families.rationale: These wrappers are not the canonical problem structures under another name: they carry additional data, a chosen `SinThetaRepresentative`. `RepresentativeProblem` says why a second structure exists; `Paper...Problem` does not.

families.title: `Block`, `Modulus`, `GraphCoordinate`, `SelectedBranch` carry the real distinction.
families.rationale: Stripping `paper` from the `paperSource*` family leaves `source*`, which is the same provenance problem in a different word. These objects live on source-coordinate block spaces, so `Block` is the information worth keeping, and the positive U -> U modulus objects should visibly say `Modulus`.

families.title: Names record mathematical scope, not review verdicts.
families.rationale: `faithful` is review terminology. The discriminator these theorems actually carry is the selected branch, so the name should say that. `paperTanTwoThetaRepresentative` is specifically a graph-coordinate operator and should say so rather than being stripped to a generic `Representative`.

moves.alternative: tanTwoTheta_orderedFormGap_symmetricNorming, if the ordered form gap is the stronger discriminator

families.title: Theorem names carrying the token mid-name are renamed in full.
families.rationale: Stripping only a leading prefix leaves names like `sineModulus_sq_add_paperCosineModulus_sq`, which is worse than either endpoint: half-converted, and now inconsistent with the object it is about. Each is renamed by applying the family decision to every object the name mentions.

Declaration-name drift clean at 1233 census declarations. All four DK checkers pass and 39 tests pass. Statement pins refreshed: 19 pins, 0 drifted, 0 warnings. The canonical-evidence digest recomputed UNCHANGED, because no canonical witness carried the prefix.
two_bugs_found_and_fixed: The first attempt applied the map to `dev/*.json`, which includes THIS document, rewriting the `current` fields it is keyed on and destroying the record of the rename. The proposal is now excluded from the target set.

The first attempt renamed `IsPaperHilbertSchmidt.comp` to `IsHilbertSchmidt.comp` while the structure itself is deferred, taking the theorem out of its namespace and breaking every `h.comp` that used dot notation. Members of a deferred namespace are now excluded, and the build caught it.

application_log.scope: 7 renames blocked by an occupied target name: the angle-family two-sided move. Applying these requires first renaming the EXISTING unprefixed declarations to their `directed*` names to vacate the target, so it is its own pass with a build after it.

7 delete/migrate decisions -- Hilbert--Schmidt into the canonical ForTauCeti API, the plane aliases into `PlanarModelSpace`, and two angle duplicates. These remove concepts rather than move names, so they are migrations with their own review, not part of a rename pass.

application_log.method: Substituted the applied stage-A map inside declaration names, longest-key-first on word boundaries, across DavisKahan/, ForTauCeti/, Challenge/, comparator/, dev/, scripts/, papers/ and docs/, excluding the two rename proposals themselves and dated snapshots.
application_log.blocked_reason: Names embedding `paperSinTwoAngleOperatorC`, `paperTanAngleOperatorC`, `paperTanTwoAngleOperatorC` or `paperHilbertSchmidt*`, whose objects stage A deliberately deferred. They resolve when stages B and C do.
application_log.verification: lake build DavisKahan.All, Challenge and ForTauCeti all exit 0; check_declaration_name_drift OK (0 findings); census render --check up to date. The 8 comparator signature failures are pre-existing: neither the old nor the new names occur anywhere in Challenge/ or comparator/, and two of the failures are in files this pass never touched.

application_log.method: One simultaneous substitution pass, longest-token-first, with underscore treated as a separator so embedded theorem names moved with their objects. Vacating and occupying in a single pass is what makes it atomic: no intermediate state exists in which a name means two things.

semantics_verified.directed: modulus and product constructions carrying acuteness hypotheses -- `directedCosAngleOperatorC = modulus (P_V ∘L P_U)`, `directedSinTwoAngleOperatorC = 2 • (directedSinAngleOperatorC * directedCosAngleOperatorC)`.
semantics_verified.canonical: literal functional calculus of the Hermitian operator angle -- `cfc Real.cos (angleOperatorC U V)`, `cfc (fun t => Real.sin (2*t)) (angleOperatorC U V)`. These now own the unqualified names, consistent with `angleOperatorC` itself.
semantics_verified.sine_needs_no_vacating: `sinAngleOperatorC = modulus (P_U - P_V)` is already the ambient sine; the literal `paperSinAngleOperatorC` is a provable duplicate and is a stage C delete, not a rename.

application_log.finding_not_in_the_review: The R and RC families had DIVERGED, and a token-level rename would have frozen the divergence. Every `*RC` variant wraps the DIRECTED complex object (`cosAngleOperatorRC` wrapped `cosAngleOperatorC`), while `tanAngleOperatorR`, `tanTwoAngleOperatorR` and `sinTwoAngleOperatorR` wrap the LITERAL ones (`paperTanAngleOperatorC` and friends). So the same stem meant different mathematics at different scalar scopes. The RC variants were therefore renamed to `directed*RC` to preserve what they actually are. Making them agree with the R family instead would mean re-pointing them at the literal objects -- a change of statement, not of name -- so it is deliberately NOT done here and is left as an open question.
application_log.suffix_normalised: `sinAngleOperatorDirectedC`/`RC` -> `directedSinAngleOperatorC`/`RC`, so the directed family spells the qualifier one way, matching `directedAngleBlockC` and `directedCosAngleBlockC`.
application_log.resolves: The 13 embedded-token names left blocked by the 2026-09-02 residue pass; `approximationNumber_paperSinTwoAngleOperatorC` is now `approximationNumber_sinTwoAngleOperatorC`.
application_log.verification: lake build DavisKahan.All, Challenge, ForTauCeti all exit 0; check_declaration_name_drift 0 findings; census render --check up to date.

application_log.review_marks: `git mv` plus a by-hand path rewrite in dev/audit/FILE-CHECKLIST.md, because `aiq-lean source checklist` does not carry marks across a rename. 711 marks before and after, and the one `[x]` on the angle module survived on its new path.

application_log.finding: A SECOND shape gap, this time in the follow-up census rather than the original. Stage A renamed the structure `IsPaperDirectRotation` to `IsDirectRotation`, and the residue census looked for that whole key inside other names. But the names that were stale embed only the inner token: `crossedDefectEquivOfPaperDirectRotation` states a fact about `IsDirectRotation`, and contains `PaperDirectRotation`, not `IsPaperDirectRotation`. Deriving the inner token from each applied rename that differs only by an `Is`/`Has` prefix reaches them.
application_log.boundary_note: These are camelCase embeddings, so the character before the token is a letter and an underscore-aware word boundary rejects them. The literal token is unambiguous because it starts with a capital, so it is substituted directly. Two boundary rules were wrong before this one: `\b` misses `_paperX`, and the underscore-aware rule misses `OfPaperX`. Each was found by checking the output, not by reasoning about the regex.

stage_status.stage_c_delete_and_migrate: plane migration applied 2026-09-02; Hilbert-Schmidt consolidation BLOCKED on a design decision, see `hilbert_schmidt_migration_assessment`

hilbert_schmidt_migration_assessment.status: not applied -- blocked on a design decision the human should make
hilbert_schmidt_migration_assessment.why_it_is_not_a_rename: DavisKahan and ForTauCeti define the same mathematics differently. `paperHilbertSchmidtEnergy A = ∑' n : ℕ, ENNReal.ofReal (approximationSingularValue n A ^ 2)` sums squared SINGULAR VALUES; ForTauCeti's `hilbertSchmidtEnergy T b = ∑' i, ‖T (b i)‖ₑ ^ 2` sums squared BASIS COLUMNS and takes the basis as an argument. They agree by a theorem, not by `rfl`.
blockers: CARRIER. `paperHilbertSchmidtNorm : ℝ` against `hilbertSchmidtENorm : ℝ≥0∞`. The 170 use sites are real inequalities inside Theorems 6.1 and 6.2 and the Sylvester theory; moving them to `ℝ≥0∞` changes source-facing statements and their arithmetic. CLAUDE.md calls a carrier difference a design question to settle, not a spelling difference, and the campaign's own rule is not to change theorem statements in a naming pass.

SCALAR SCOPE. The bridge is complex-only while the definitions are `RCLike`-generic. `hilbertSchmidtEnergy_eq_basisEnergy` is stated for `HilbertBasis ι ℂ F` and `A : F →L[ℂ] E`, and the whole bridge file is ℂ throughout (70 occurrences of ℂ, none of `RCLike`), while `HilbertSchmidt.lean` carrying the definitions is `RCLike` throughout (21 occurrences). A complete migration needs the bridge generalized to `RCLike` first, which is foundational work, not renaming.
hilbert_schmidt_migration_assessment.what_is_already_proved: The correspondence itself: `hilbertSchmidtEnergy_eq_basisEnergy` gives basis-independence, `hilbertSchmidtENorm_eq_ofReal_paperHilbertSchmidtNorm` and the `IsPaperHilbertSchmidt` iff are proved at ℂ. So the migration is feasible; it is a decision and a generalization away, not an unknown.
hilbert_schmidt_migration_assessment.scale: 370 use sites across 18 files, including Theorem61, Theorem62, Section6AppendixLeakage and four Sylvester modules.
hilbert_schmidt_migration_assessment.recommendation: Settle the carrier first. If the source-facing statements should keep `ℝ`, ForTauCeti needs an `ℝ`-valued norm alongside the `ℝ≥0∞` one and the migration is then mechanical. If they should move to `ℝ≥0∞`, that is a deliberate change to Theorems 6.1 and 6.2 and should be reviewed as such. Renaming the DavisKahan names instead -- to say they are the singular-value definition -- is explicitly what the review did not want, since it would preserve a competing concept under a better name.
